title: Code and data for: The second normal-stress coefficient sets the regularity boundary of the Reiner-Rivlin rotating-disk similarity reduction
description:
Python code, numerical data and figures that reproduce every numerical result in the manuscript The second normal-stress coefficient sets the regularity boundary of the Reiner-Rivlin rotating-disk similarity reduction, submitted to the Journal of Non-Newtonian Fluid Mechanics.

The archive covers: the identification of the Reiner-Rivlin cross-viscosity with the second normal-stress coefficient; the negative-K regularity boundary and its closed form lambda_c = 1/(2K), checked over eleven (K, S) cases; the Weissenberg-number collapse 2 Wi2 |lambda_c| = 1; the symbolic comparison with the second-order fluid; the temporal stability analysis by direct generalised eigensolve, with independent time-integration checks and mode tracking; the map of the stability threshold against the regularity boundary over ten values of K; the species-block spectrum; and the inviscid Gregory-Stuart-Walker crossflow diagnostic; and the conditioning and coefficient-level singularity diagnostic near the regularity boundary.

The README lists the scripts and the values each one reproduces. REFERENCE_VERIFICATION.md records how each citation was checked, and DEVELOPMENT_HISTORY.md records how the analysis evolved, including the numerical errors found and corrected along the way.
